title: Oven Sensor Open
shortDescription: The oven temperature sensor reads open circuit.
fullDescription:
E1 is posted when the RTD at the rear of the oven cavity reads infinite resistance. Heating is disabled until the sensor is replaced.

The sensor plug is usually at the back of the oven behind the rear panel.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the RTD at the rear of the oven.

faq.a: No - the oven will refuse to heat.

title: Oven Sensor Shorted
shortDescription: The oven temperature sensor reads shorted.
fullDescription:
E2 is the shorted-sensor counterpart of E1. The RTD or its wiring reads near zero ohms, indicating an impossibly high temperature.

Replace the sensor and inspect the harness for pinching.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new RTD and inspect wiring.

whenToCallPro: If harness damage is inside foam.

title: Over-temperature
fullDescription:
E3 is raised when the RTD reads above the allowed maximum. A welded bake relay or a control fault leaves the heater on.

Turn the breaker off immediately and call service.

title: Door Lock Fault
shortDescription: The self-clean lock did not reach its commanded position.
fullDescription:
E4 appears when the lock motor is commanded and the limit switch does not confirm. A seized motor, broken cam, or bad switch cause E4.

Do not force a locked door.
whenToCallPro: If door is locked with hot contents.

faq.a: Use the control cancel; E4 posts if the lock does not return.

title: Door Switch Fault
shortDescription: Door switch reports an invalid state.
fullDescription:
E5 is posted when the door switch reads closed while the lock says open or vice versa. A failed switch or loose harness are the usual causes.

Replace the switch after continuity testing.

fixSteps.title: Test
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity as the switch is pressed.

title: Cooling Fan Fault
shortDescription: Cooling fan not running at tacho-expected speed.
fullDescription:
E6 is raised if the cooling fan tacho is absent or slow. Dust, worn bearing, or failed motor are typical causes.

The fan protects the control panel area from heat.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new cooling fan motor.

whenToCallPro: If fan is fine but E6 still posts.

title: Meat Probe Fault
shortDescription: Meat probe reads out of valid range.
fullDescription:
E7 appears when the meat probe reads open or shorted. A new probe or a clean jack usually fixes it.

If not using the probe, remove it to clear the code.

fixSteps.title: Remove probe
fixSteps.instruction: Pull probe and clean the jack.

whenToCallPro: If jack or board needs service.

title: Stuck Touch Key
shortDescription: A touch key reads pressed continuously.
fullDescription:
E8 is posted when a key stays active longer than allowed. Liquid, food, or a cracked glass cause it.

Clean and power cycle; replace the panel if it persists.

faq.a: Water in the panel - let dry fully.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Touch panel and main board not communicating.
fullDescription:
E9 indicates lost serial link between boards. Loose ribbon or failed board are the usual causes.

Reseat ribbon after a power cycle.

title: EEPROM Fault
fullDescription: E10 signals EEPROM read/write failure. A service-mode reload sometimes works; otherwise the control board must be replaced with one preloaded for the model.

faq.a: User resets do not restore EEPROM.
